newsitem.title: UK: Metals Outlook - June pricing to set market tone.
newsitem.headline: Metals Outlook - June pricing to set market tone.

text.p: Base metal markets are set for another excitable week on the London Metal Exchange (LME), with Monday's action focusing on "third Wednesday" pricing.
The copper market will remain the centre of activity, with prices residing just under $2,600 after hitting 13-month highs last weekend.
"The only thing you can say with any certainty is that it is going to be volatile," said Angus MacMillan, analyst at LME trader Billiton Metals Ltd.
"It can do anything (Monday). It all depends on what way the cash pricing goes, and whether it is net long or short," a trader said.
Copper hit its highs of $2,609 last Thursday, when talk swirled around the market of a Far Eastern firm running up huge trading losses, partly related to options business.
On Friday, however, some of the steam came out of the market, with profit-taking seen around $2,600, and by the end of the week prices were back to $2,570.
"We have had a bit of consolidation, but it still looks good on the upside," said William Adams of LME trader Rudolf Wolff and Co.
On the fundamental side, concerns persisted over supply, with copper production down at Inco Sudbury in Canada due to the strike there.
Reduced gas supplies to Russia's Norilsk were hitting metal production there, and Papua New Guineau's OK Tedi was unable to ship concentrates due to low water levels on the River Fly, traders said.
Offsetting all that, the giant Kennecott smelter in the U.S. was now running near capacity after a successful maintenance closure recently.
Analysts said that once the current tight supply picture eased, fundamental oversupply would dominate the copper market.
"Production in the second half will be considerably higher than in the first half of the year and production in 1998 will be higher than this year," Billiton's MacMillan said.
Pricing against the June date would also dictate events in the aluminium market, which suffered on Friday from pre-emptive sales of that nature, traders said.
More cash sales could accentuate the retreat from $1,600, although there were some significant shorts against the monthly prompt, others noted.
Elsewhere, a strong zinc market looked set to chase higher and notch up further 4-1/2 year highs, although traders would be watching to see if the stock increases seen late last week became a trend.
"A further rise in Singapore stocks all but confirms last months fears that the Chinese were going to deliver sizeable quantities into Singapore," Wolff's Adams said.
Nickel's performance would be influenced by the stoppage at Inco and possible losses at Norilsk, although those factors might be fading as supportive, some said.
